utterances.text: Can you also tell the Court the name of your younger brother and the name of your older brother?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Hajrudin, my younger brother, stayed on after me in Susica. He was born in 1967. My older brother, Hakija, was born in 1962. He was married to Dragica Sokic, a Serb woman. I last saw him when I was taken to Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Where any -- because you mention your younger brother stayed in Susica after you. How many, if any, members of your family were held in detention in Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Out of my family members, in addition to my brother Hakija who was married to a Serb woman and he had to report to the police station every 24 hours and he was detained in the police station, my entire family went through the Susica camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And were the remains of your younger brother ever found?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were found. He was found at three locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Do you know the name of these locations or -- and did you participate in the identification process?

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: Kljestani 1 and Kljestani 2. I took part in the identification process, and I also took part in the identification process for my sister, as we were looking for her.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, do you think you can describe for the Court how the experience of losing so many members of your family and also being detained has affected you.

utterances.speaker: IBRO OSMANOVIC
utterances.text: The loss of family members is something that is the hardest of all. It is easy to look for someone that you're not related to, who is not your family. But to rummage through the bones of someone who was born by your very own mother, I mean, my sister was only 16 years old, and there are only four bones left of her. It's very hard to speak about something like that. It wasn't that hard for me to look for them. It was important for me to find them. And I managed to find two of them after all these years, and I don't know if I'll manage to find the third one.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Osmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. I only have one aerial photo of the Susica camp that I would like to show to the witness. It is already in evidence, but I would like him to make some markings. But I can leave it for tomorrow. Besides that, my examination is -- will be concluded after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we do that tomorrow in order not to -- because it usually takes at least a couple of minutes and then ... Mr. Osmanovic, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate with anyone about the testimony you have given today or the testimony you are still about to give tomorrow. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I make one observation. I'm addressing you, Ms. D'Ascoli, but it happened to other counsel as well. Would you please carefully not only focus on your questions but also listen to the answers. To ask to a witness whether the remains of his younger brother were found, if, two minutes ago, he has told us that the head was found at 25 kilometres from the rest, is not something which avoids further painful experience. I do understand that if you want to know the location of the mass graves that you should inquire into which three places, but to ask him were the remains found, it may sound, in the ears of the witness, as you have not listened to his answer very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Friday, the 21st of September, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 21st day of September, 2012, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.16 p.m.,
